correctness.rationale: The projected half-diameter is the maximum support quadratic form on the random hyperplane, whose excess over the baseline squared semiaxis is the largest eigenvalue of a two-by-two rank-two Gram compression. Exact determinant algebra gives one quadratic inequality in the first two squared normal coordinates. The Haar radial-angle decomposition has S~Beta(1,(d-2)/2); conditioning proves the all-d CDF and strict stochastic ordering. In four dimensions S is uniform, the rational integral evaluates to a fixed artanh and differentiates to the claimed affine-skew arcsine density. The inequality atanh(r)<r/(1-r^2) proves positive mixture weights. The smooth simple top eigenvalue, fixed A>B>0 gap and Gaussian spherical representation imply the chi-square limit. The bundled verifier independently checked 1960 exact rational polynomial identities, 76 closed-vs-quadrature values, 700 directly compressed matrix eigenvalues, 24 Monte Carlo CDF points and 6 dimension orderings; finite tests are not substitutes for proof.

originality.rationale: No equivalent rank-two Haar hyperplane-shadow maximal-radius CDF or four-dimensional affine-skew arcsine beta mixture was found in directly queried public mathematical records or in the material read from closest sources. Guedon et al. and Hinrichs et al. treat central sections and asymptotic/high-probability radius estimates, not orthogonal-shadow beta mixtures. The closest exact one-spike result treats rank-one central sections; it does not imply the rank-two projected eigenvalue distribution from its stated result. Prior statistical rank-two compression theory remains a genuine historical-priority risk, so novelty is provisional rather than a uniqueness certificate.
residual_risks: A rank-two orthogonal-compression eigenvalue CDF could have appeared in older multivariate statistics or projected-ellipsoid tomography with different terminology; finite targeted searches cannot establish priority exhaustively.
The stated high-dimensional chi-square limit assumes fixed A>B>0; collapsing spike gaps are not addressed.

value.rationale: The random maximal radius of an ellipsoid shadow is a standard, geometrically motivated size statistic and the first unequal two-spike case has genuinely coupled coordinates, unlike rank-one beta transforms. The four-dimensional exact density simplifies unexpectedly to a nontrivial two-component beta mixture with positive, shape-controlled weights; this gives the entire distribution and sharp support for a natural fully variable three-length ellipsoid family. The same derivation yields an exact law in every dimension, strict stochastic dimension monotonicity and a universal limiting fluctuation. It is a complete structural determination of a natural nontrivial invariant, not a known-table recomputation, arbitrary parameter slice or unsupported algorithmic check.
